sequence_reshape.note: Each 30-feature transaction vector is reshaped into (6 timesteps x 5 features): Time+V1-V4, V5-V9, V10-V14, V15-V19, V20-V24, V25-V28+Amount. This is an artificial sequence — the dataset has no genuine per-customer transaction ordering.

imbalance_handling: SMOTE (imblearn.over_sampling.SMOTE, random_state=42) applied to the training split only
data_caveat: IMPORTANT — not yet on the shared pipeline: this run's data-loading cell falls back to a synthetic dataset (28,492 rows, 492 synthetic 'fraud' cases) whenever creditcard.csv isn't found at runtime, instead of loading the shared data/processed/{train,val,test}.csv splits used by MLP, TabNet, and CNN-1D. It also uses SMOTE instead of the class-weighting approach the other three models share. Point the data-loading cell at the shared processed CSVs, remove the SMOTE step (or justify keeping it), and re-run before these hyperparameters/results are treated as directly comparable to the other three models (see report Section 7.3 and 7.6).
